pages.label: Google: SUBSCRIPTION_PURCHASED
pages.title: What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_PURCHASED mean?
pages.description: SUBSCRIPTION_PURCHASED (4) means a new subscription was purchased. Fetch its state, grant access and acknowledge it within three days or Google refunds it.
pages.answer: The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_PURCHASED means a new subscription was purchased and has a new purchase token.
facts: Sent by
Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint
causes: A customer bought a subscription in your app or in the Play Store.
A resubscribe after the old subscription expired is a new purchase with a brand new purchase token and no `linkedPurchaseToken`.
An upgrade, downgrade or signup after cancelling from your app creates a new token with `linkedPurchaseToken` pointing to the old one.
fixes: Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
Call `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`, check `subscriptionState` is `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_ACTIVE`, and grant access.
Acknowledge the purchase within three days. Google says an unacknowledged purchase is refunded and revoked automatically.
Use `linkedPurchaseToken` or `outOfAppPurchaseContext` to connect the new token to the right customer.
Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.
pages.mapping: RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. A token RevenueDot has not stored gives an `INITIAL_PURCHASE` event; a replacement token joins the customer of its `linkedPurchaseToken`, and the old chain ends with a `PRODUCT_CHANGE` event instead of a `CANCELLATION` or `EXPIRATION`. RevenueDot acknowledges the purchase itself, and if that fails it answers 5xx so Pub/Sub retries.

pages.label: Google: SUBSCRIPTION_RENEWED
pages.title: What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_RENEWED mean?
pages.description: SUBSCRIPTION_RENEWED (2) means an active subscription renewed. Fetch the new expiry time and extend access. Renewals need no acknowledgement.
pages.answer: The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_RENEWED means an active subscription renewed for another period.
facts: Sent by
Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint
causes: The renewal charge succeeded on the billing date.
For installment subscriptions, Google sends it each time a payment is charged on its billing date.
Renewals do not need to be acknowledged.
fixes: Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
Check the customer is still entitled, then store the new `expiryTime` from the subscription resource.
Do not acknowledge a renewal: Google says it is not needed.
Keep the order ID (`latestOrderId`), which is new for every renewal.
Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.
pages.mapping: RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. A new order on the token gives a `RENEWAL` event, with `is_trial_conversion: true` when the previous period was a free trial. Renewal order IDs carry a `..N` suffix, which is how RevenueDot tells a renewal order from the first.

pages.label: Google: SUBSCRIPTION_CANCELED
pages.title: What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_CANCELED mean?
pages.description: SUBSCRIPTION_CANCELED (3) means a subscription was cancelled by the customer, you or the system. Access continues to the expiry time; do not remove it early.
pages.answer: The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_CANCELED means a subscription was cancelled, but the customer keeps access until the paid period ends.
facts: Sent by
Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint
pages.definition: A subscription was cancelled, voluntarily or involuntarily. For a voluntary cancellation, it is sent when the user cancels.
causes: The customer cancelled in the Play subscriptions center, you cancelled with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.cancel`, or the subscription was cancelled after account hold ran out.

The subscription resource then has `subscriptionState` `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_CANCELED`, and `expiryTime` says when access ends. If that time is already past, for example after a cancel during account hold, access ends now.
`canceledStateContext` says who cancelled and `userInitiatedCancellation` can say why.
fixes: Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
Keep access until `expiryTime`. Google warns that removing access a customer is still entitled to violates its subscriptions policy.
Show a message with the end date and a way to resubscribe.
Read `canceledStateContext` to choose your win-back message.
Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.
pages.mapping: RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot stores the purchase as unsubscribed and sends `CANCELLATION`. The `cancel_reason` is `DEVELOPER_INITIATED` when Google says you cancelled it, `BILLING_ERROR` or `PRICE_INCREASE` when the system did, and `UNSUBSCRIBE` otherwise. A cancellation caused by an upgrade or downgrade is not a customer cancellation and is skipped. The `EXPIRATION` event comes later.

pages.label: Google: SUBSCRIPTION_ON_HOLD
pages.title: What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_ON_HOLD mean?
pages.description: SUBSCRIPTION_ON_HOLD (5) means a subscription entered account hold after a payment failure. Block access and ask the customer to fix their payment method.
pages.answer: The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_ON_HOLD means a renewal payment failed and the subscription is now in account hold, so access should stop.
facts: Sent by
Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint
pages.definition: A subscription has entered account hold, if account hold is enabled.
causes: A renewal payment failed and any grace period has ended. Account hold then begins. Google's default is 60 days minus the grace period.
A subscription resuming from a pause with a failed payment goes straight into account hold.
During hold the `expiryTime` stays in the past and the customer should not have access.
fixes: Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
Block access to the subscription while it is on hold.
Ask the customer to fix their payment method. Google tells customers too.
When they do, you get `SUBSCRIPTION_RECOVERED` with the same purchase token. If they do not, the subscription is cancelled and expires.
Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.
pages.mapping: RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot stores a billing issue and ends access now. It sends `BILLING_ISSUE` and a `CANCELLATION` with `cancel_reason: BILLING_ERROR`, and the scheduler sends `EXPIRATION` with `expiration_reason: BILLING_ERROR`. A recovery later comes out as `RENEWAL`.

pages.label: Google: SUBSCRIPTION_IN_GRACE_PERIOD
pages.title: What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_IN_GRACE_PERIOD mean?
pages.description: SUBSCRIPTION_IN_GRACE_PERIOD (6) means a renewal payment failed and the subscription entered its grace period. Keep access and prompt the customer to fix payment.
pages.answer: The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_IN_GRACE_PERIOD means a renewal payment failed, but the customer keeps access during the grace period.
facts: Sent by
Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint
pages.definition: A subscription has entered the grace period, if the grace period is enabled.
causes: A renewal payment failed and the base plan has a grace period. Google enables it by default on auto-renewing base plans.
Google waits at least one day before the notification even with a grace period of zero days, to leave time for payment retries.
The subscription resource has state `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_IN_GRACE_PERIOD` and `expiryTime` stays in the past until the grace period ends, but entitlement should last.
fixes: Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
Keep access while the grace period runs.
Encourage the customer to fix their payment method, with a message in your app.
Expect `SUBSCRIPTION_RECOVERED` or `SUBSCRIPTION_RENEWED` on success, or `SUBSCRIPTION_ON_HOLD` when the grace period ends.
Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.
pages.mapping: RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot stores a billing issue with the grace period end set to the line item's expiry, so access continues. It sends `BILLING_ISSUE` with `grace_period_expiration_at_ms` and a `CANCELLATION` with `cancel_reason: BILLING_ERROR`. If access later ends, `EXPIRATION` follows.

pages.label: Google: SUBSCRIPTION_RESTARTED
pages.title: What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_RESTARTED mean?
pages.description: SUBSCRIPTION_RESTARTED (7) means the customer restored a cancelled subscription from Play before it expired. It keeps its purchase token and renews again.
pages.answer: The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_RESTARTED means a customer undid a cancellation before the subscription expired.
facts: Sent by
Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint
pages.definition: The user restored their subscription from Play, Account, Subscriptions. The subscription was cancelled but had not expired when the user restored it.
causes: The customer tapped Resubscribe on a cancelled subscription that was still running. Google calls this a restore.
The same purchase token continues and all cancellation fields are cleared.
After expiry the same action is a new purchase and arrives as `SUBSCRIPTION_PURCHASED`.
fixes: Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
Record that the subscription is set to renew again and stop showing restore messages.
Do not grant anything new: the customer already has access until `expiryTime`.
Stop your win-back flow for this customer.
Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.
pages.mapping: RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. The cancellation is cleared on the stored purchase and RevenueDot sends `UNCANCELLATION`.

pages.label: Google: SUBSCRIPTION_RECOVERED
pages.title: What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_RECOVERED mean?
pages.description: SUBSCRIPTION_RECOVERED (1) means a subscription recovered from account hold or resumed from a pause. Restore access and extend it to the new expiry time.
pages.answer: The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_RECOVERED means a subscription came back from account hold or from a pause.
facts: Sent by
Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint
pages.definition: A subscription was recovered from account hold or resumed from a pause.
causes: The customer fixed their payment method during account hold, and the retried payment worked. The purchase token stays the same.
A paused subscription resumed, at the end of the pause or because the customer resumed it by hand.
The billing date moves to the recovery date.
fixes: Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
Restore access and extend it to the new `expiryTime`.
Remove any fix-payment or paused message in your app.
Do not count it as a new subscriber.
Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.
pages.mapping: RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. A new order on a token whose access had ended is Google renewing it, so RevenueDot moves the stored end to now and sends `RENEWAL`, not a new purchase and not `UNCANCELLATION`.

pages.label: Google: SUBSCRIPTION_DEFERRED
pages.title: What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_DEFERRED mean?
pages.description: SUBSCRIPTION_DEFERRED (9) means a subscription's billing date was pushed later with the defer API. The customer keeps full access and is not charged during the deferral.
pages.answer: The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_DEFERRED means the billing date of a subscription was moved later, so the customer gets more time without a charge.
facts: Sent by
Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint
pages.definition: A subscription's recurrence time has been extended.
causes: Your backend called `purchases.subscriptionsv2.defer`, for example for a free week as a promotion or a goodwill gesture.
During the deferral the customer has full access and is not charged. The renewal date is updated.
For prepaid plans the defer API moves the expiration time.
fixes: Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
Store the new `expiryTime` and extend access to it.
Record why the deferral was given, so support can explain it.
Do not treat it as a payment.
Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.
pages.mapping: RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. The period start is unchanged and the end moves later, so RevenueDot sends `SUBSCRIPTION_EXTENDED`. No money moves on it: its `price` is 0.

pages.description: SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSE_SCHEDULE_CHANGED (11) means a customer scheduled or changed a pause. Access continues until the next renewal date; the pause starts then.

Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint
pages.definition: A subscription pause schedule has been changed.
causes: The customer chose to pause in Play. A pause takes effect only after the current billing period ends.
The subscription is still `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_ACTIVE` and `autoRenewEnabled` is true. The customer keeps access until the next renewal date.
Pause lengths run from one week to three months depending on the recurrence.

Keep access until the renewal date and show that a pause is coming.
When the pause starts, you get `SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED`.
Offer a way to resume by deep link to Google Play.

A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot reads the scheduled resume time from the version 1 subscription API and stores it as the auto-resume date while the subscription is still active. Remove access until the subscription resumes.
Show the expected resume date from `pausedStateContext`.
Wait for `SUBSCRIPTION_RECOVERED` when it resumes, or `SUBSCRIPTION_ON_HOLD` if the payment fails on resume.

pages.title: What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_REVOKED mean?
pages.description: SUBSCRIPTION_REVOKED (12) means a subscription was revoked before its expiry, for example by you or by a chargeback. Remove access at once.
pages.answer: The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_REVOKED means a subscription was taken away before its expiration time, so access must end now.

Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint

The subscription resource has `subscriptionState` set to `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_EXPIRED`.
Unlike a cancellation, the customer does not keep access to the period end.

Revoke the customer's entitlement immediately.
Record the revocation for support and refund reports.
Offer a new subscription if the revocation was in error.

A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. pages.title: What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRED mean?
pages.description: SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRED (13) means a subscription has expired. Confirm the state is expired, then remove the entitlement.
pages.answer: The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRED means a subscription has run out and the customer should lose access.
facts: Sent by
Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint
causes: The paid period ended after a cancellation, or account hold ran out.
The subscription resource has `subscriptionState` `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_EXPIRED` and `expiryTime` in the past.
A revoked subscription also reads as expired.
fixes: Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
Confirm `subscriptionState` is `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_EXPIRED`, then remove the entitlement.
Mark the purchase as no longer valid in your backend.
Keep the customer's data, since they can resubscribe, which is a new purchase.
Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.
pages.mapping: RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot stores the purchase as ended and as unsubscribed (a `CANCELLATION` if none had been sent). The `EXPIRATION` event is recorded once by the scheduler when access, grace included, has ended, with the reason from the stored state.

pages.description: ONE_TIME_PRODUCT_PURCHASED (1) means a one-time product was bought. Fetch the purchase, deliver the item once and acknowledge or consume it.
pages.answer: The Google Play notification ONE_TIME_PRODUCT_PURCHASED means a customer bought a one-time product.
facts: Sent by
Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint
pages.definition: A one-time product was successfully purchased by a user.
causes: A customer completed the purchase of an in-app product.
Google sends it only if you chose to receive one-time product purchase events when you set up notifications.
The message carries the `sku` and the `purchaseToken`.
fixes: Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
Call the products API with the `sku` and token, check the purchase state, and deliver the item once.
Acknowledge or consume the purchase so Google does not refund it.
Key delivery on the order so a repeat message does not give the item twice.
Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

RevenueDot fetches the product purchase for the `sku` and token, skips a purchase that is still pending, stores it under its order ID and acknowledges it. A new purchase gives `NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE`. The consumable flag comes from the product's type in your catalog.

pages.label: Google: VOIDED_PURCHASE
pages.title: What does the Google Play notification VOIDED_PURCHASE mean?
pages.description: A voidedPurchaseNotification means Google voided a purchase: a refund, chargeback or revocation. Revoke the item or access using the order ID and refund type.
pages.answer: A Google Play voidedPurchaseNotification means a purchase was voided, usually by a refund or a chargeback, so what it granted should be taken back.
facts: Sent by
Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint
pages.definition: A purchase has been voided. The message gives the purchase token, the order ID, the product type (subscription or one-time) and the refund type (full or quantity-based partial).
causes: The customer was refunded, charged back, or you revoked the purchase.
`productType` 1 is a subscription and 2 a one-time product. `refundType` 1 is a full refund and 2 a quantity-based partial refund of a multi-quantity purchase.
For subscriptions, a new order ID is created for each renewal, so the order ID says which period was voided.
fixes: Find the purchase by `purchaseToken` and `orderId` and revoke what that order granted.
For a partial refund, adjust the quantity instead of revoking everything. `refundableQuantity` in the products API gives what is left.
For more data, use Google's Voided Purchases API, a pull model over a time range.
Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.
pages.mapping: RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. For a subscription RevenueDot marks the voided period refunded (only if the order is the current one) and sends `CANCELLATION` with `cancel_reason: CUSTOMER_SUPPORT` and a negative price. A one-time purchase is marked refunded the same way. A partial quantity refund (`refundType` 2) of a one-time product is ignored. A daily scan of Google's voided purchases catches refunds whose message never arrived.
